statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail edges up one point inside the low band as the US-Iran memorandum lapses today, while the observed price path stays two-way: the overnight high at 30,331.50 was retraced about 62 points and then bought back without a new high, leaving the band unchanged at roughly 0.56%.
recommendation: Overnight conditions remain consistent with a mean-reverting regime. NQ has recovered its pullback to within about 20 points of the 30,331.50 overnight high but has not extended through it, so the range top has now been tested twice without a breakout and the band is unchanged at about 0.56%. Cross-asset confirmation is still absent, with Dow futures marginally negative, latest-session software breadth negative against strong semiconductors, and crude fading from 89.30 despite Hormuz transits reported at zero on Sunday. The lapse of the US-Iran memorandum today is a genuine discontinuity checkpoint, but it is not currently transmitting into energy or volatility pricing. The mapped policy state is EA_ON, with a narrow danger window flagged around the US cash open and its first hour.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures at 30,311.25, back within 20 points of the 30,331.50 overnight high without extending it, as the US-Iran memorandum lapses with Brent at 88.85 and the VIX near 14.9
body: NQ futures trade near 30,311.25, about 0.56% above the 30,141.75 prior settlement, inside an observed overnight band of roughly 30,163.75-30,331.50. The development since the previous assessment is structural: the roughly 62-point retracement off the 30,331.50 high has been bought back to within about 20 points of that extreme, but no new high has printed and the band is unchanged at about 0.56% width. The range top has therefore been tested twice and rejected twice, and a completed retracement has been fully recovered without extension. That is two-way behaviour, not a failed-retracement sequence, and no repeated extension is observed. Cross-asset confirmation remains absent and is arguably weaker than an hour ago: delayed context shows S&P 500 futures up about 0.14% and Dow futures negative at -0.17% against NQ at +0.56%, so the advance is narrow and index-specific. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Friday at 30,046.14, down 0.13% inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range, after the S&P 500 slipped from a record high but capped a third consecutive weekly gain. The VIX is near 14.94, up about 4.8% on the day but still close to the 2026 lows below 14.4 printed last week, while VIX futures are marginally lower, a conflict that argues for uncertainty rather than for directional risk. The dominant stress channel is the Gulf conflict, and it reached a scheduled inflection today: the 60-day US-Iran memorandum of understanding governing safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz expired with neither side willing to extend it, both having accused the other of violations, and with the Treasury Secretary signalling new sanctions within days. Ship-tracking data cited on Monday showed five commodity vessels transiting the Strait on Saturday and none on Sunday, against 31 the prior weekend. Crude nonetheless continues to discount rather than amplify that disruption: Brent traded as high as 89.30 and now trades near 88.85, up about 0.38%, while WTI slipped below 82 to near 82.21, down about 0.23%, with the absence of a major supply outage limiting further gains. That refusal of energy to price a discontinuity is the single most informative cross-asset observation available this hour. Rates remain supportive, with the H.15 series for 13 August showing the 2-year at 4.15% and the 10-year at 4.63%, the 10-year cash yield near 4.68-4.70% at Friday's close, Treasury futures modestly bid overnight, and a September Fed hike priced near 30% after soft retail sales at -0.6% month-over-month and weakening consumer sentiment. Latest-session internals are split rather than aligned: semiconductors were uniformly positive with a mean gain near 1.9%, led by Micron, Intel and Arm, and seven of eight megacaps advanced, but software-infrastructure and software-application breadth was negative, so the tech complex is rotating internally rather than moving as one. A compressed and unchanged index range, a fully recovered retracement, absent cross-asset confirmation, fading crude and no Tier-1 US release today keep tail risk in the low band, with a single point added for the genuine discontinuity checkpoint that the memorandum lapse represents. Scheduled checkpoints today are the medium-impact Empire State survey at 12:30Z, consensus near 10.2 against a 15.6 prior, and the NAHB index at 14:00Z. The principal structural checkpoint remains the 13:30Z cash open, where opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would be the specific pattern capable of denying mean reversion; that structure is not observed in advance. FOMC minutes on 19 August at 18:00Z and the Home Depot, Target and Walmart results across Tuesday to Thursday are the week's main scheduled catalysts.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Tail stayed in the low band throughout, ranging from 12 to 17, with the mapped policy state EA_ON for the entire window. Stress peaked at 82 during Sunday's US-hours window as Gulf conflict and crude headlines dominated, then eased steadily to 65 by the final hour as the tape compressed and crude began to fade. Dominant mode was mixed through the weekend session, settled to normal from 23:00Z as two-way overnight rotation established itself, and returned to mixed from 06:00Z as NQ decoupled from a flat broader futures complex.
outlookSummary: The conditional path keeps tail in the low band across all 24 forecast hours, with the mapped policy state EA_ON throughout. Conditional risk holds at 14 through the European morning, lifts into the 12:00Z hour containing the Empire State survey, and peaks at 17 across the 13:00Z-14:00Z window covering the US cash open, the opening auction and the NAHB release, which is the point at which opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would first become observable. It decays through the US afternoon as opening imbalances clear, lifts again to 16 into the 19:00Z power hour and the 20:00Z cash close where late continuation or reversal can be sharp, then falls to a daily minimum of 13 across the thin post-close and Asian hours before drifting back to 14 into Tuesday's European session. Stress eases from 66 toward 63 overnight, with a temporary lift to 70 across the US open window, and remains elevated throughout because the Gulf shipping channel is headline-driven rather than scheduled. Confidence decays steadily with forecast distance because current price-path evidence cannot be extended reliably across a full day.
